sections.html:
Eagle Mountain is in northwest Utah County, in the flat Cedar Valley west and north of the Lake Mountains, and it belongs to the Provo-Orem metro area. The city covers about 50 square miles at roughly 4,885 feet. Because it is in Utah County, your tax bill, deed recording and property records all run through Provo. The county treasurer and recorder both work from the county building at 100 East Center Street.

The city grew fast: 2,157 residents in 2000, 21,415 in 2010, 43,623 in 2020 and an estimated 66,557 in mid-2025. Homes are mostly owner-occupied at 84.7%, the median home value is $518,100, median gross rent is $2,020, and the average household has 4.18 people. Data centers are the most visible employer here, and ongoing construction and hiring keep newcomers looking for homes.

sections.h2: Which school district will serve the house?
sections.html:
The Alpine School District serves Eagle Mountain now, and that changes on July 1, 2027, when the district splits into three. Eagle Mountain, Saratoga Springs, Cedar Fort and Fairfield will form the Lake Mountain School District. Lehi, American Fork, Highland, Alpine and Cedar Hills go to Aspen Peaks, and Orem, Pleasant Grove, Lindon and Vineyard go to Timpanogos.

Current schools include eight elementary schools, Frontier Middle School and Cedar Valley High School, which opened in August 2019, plus charter schools such as The Ranches Academy, John Hancock Charter School and Rockwell Charter High School. If you sell during the transition, expect buyers to ask which district the address will land in, and send them to the district office for boundary maps.

The main routes are SR-73, Pony Express Parkway, Eagle Mountain Boulevard and Ranches Parkway. The Mountain View Corridor segment linking the Salt Lake and Utah valleys was completed in December 2025, and UTA has run express bus Route 806 since 2008.

Rainfall is light, about 16.75 inches a year in the Ranches area. The city center is drier and cooler with colder nights, and the combined average July high is 90 degrees. Buyers usually ask for the roof's age, so have that date handy.

Eagle Mountain allows accessory dwelling units, but not in townhomes, duplexes or apartments, and an ADU permit is required on top of any building permit.

  • The unit needs its own kitchen, bathroom and separate entrance.
  • The owner must live in either the main home or the ADU, with temporary absences allowed.
  • The site plan must show two off-street parking spaces.
  • The application fee is $230.
  • ADUs cannot be rented for fewer than 30 consecutive days.

Unpermitted units are treated as illegal until an application is approved. Short-term rentals of any kind also carry a 1% transient room tax under city code, with records kept for at least three years. Unpaid amounts add a 10% penalty and 12% annual interest, and the operator's business license can be revoked.

sections.h2: Property tax dates and deed recording
sections.html:
Utah County sets the calendar, and every date below comes from the county.

Utah County property tax dates
EventWhen
Valuation notices mailed by the AuditorAround July 22
Board of Equalization appeals dueSeptember 1
Tax notices mailedThird week of October
Real property taxes dueNovember 30
Delinquent parcels chargedDecember 1, greater of $10 or 1%

Mailed payments count if they carry a U.S. Post Office postmark, but a postage meter mark from an office does not. Utah also gives a 45% primary residential exemption, so tax is based on 55% of a primary home's value.

Deeds are recorded with the Utah County Recorder in Provo, which charges a $40 standard fee per document plus $2 for each description over ten. Credit and debit cards carry a 2.65% processing fee, while electronic checks do not.

sections.h2: Selling a house with an ADU or basement unit
sections.html:
Many Eagle Mountain houses have a finished basement, and some have a second unit. Whether you can sell it as a legal rental depends on the permit. A unit with an approved ADU permit, its own kitchen, bathroom and separate entrance, and two off-street parking spaces on the site plan is a selling point. A unit without one is treated as illegal until an application is approved, and a lender may refuse to count it.

If you did apply, keep the receipt or the approval. If you rented the house for stays under 30 days, keep the transient room tax records for at least three years, because unpaid amounts add a 10% penalty and 12% annual interest. A buyer's title company may ask about both, and having the answer ready helps the sale.

You do not have to settle every question before you sell for cash. You do need to describe the unit honestly, so the buyer can price the house for what it is.

sections.h2: Appeals, taxes and the closing statement
sections.html:
If you think your valuation is too high, the Board of Equalization deadline is September 1, set by the county. After that date the value stands for the year, so a closing in the fall cannot reopen it. The Auditor's notice, mailed around July 22, is the paper to keep.

At closing the title company divides the year's tax between you and the buyer and pays any unpaid balance from your proceeds. Ask for that line to be shown separately on the closing statement. If you mail a payment before closing, use a U.S. Post Office postmark, since a postage meter mark from an office does not count.

sections.h2: What to gather before you talk to a buyer
sections.html:
A short folder of papers saves days later. Start with the parcel number from your Utah County tax notice, since every county lookup depends on it.

  • The most recent tax notice and proof of payment.
  • The ADU permit or the application receipt, if the house has a second unit.
  • Transient room tax records, if you ever rented the house for stays under 30 days.
  • Any HOA contact, loan payoff details and the roof's age.

Pull any HOA documents too. Buyers often want to know about dues and rules before they sign, and a quick call to the HOA contact gets you the figures you need.

If you are unsure whether an ADU or a basement unit was ever permitted, ask the city before you list. The answer decides whether a financed buyer can close.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Eagle Mountain?
sections.html:
A cash sale means no mortgage underwriting, so closing depends on title work alone.

  1. Send the address and a few details about the house.
  2. We review the property and nearby sales.
  3. You accept or decline the offer.
  4. A title company prepares the paperwork and sets a closing date.
  5. The deed is recorded in Provo and you are paid at closing.

A house with an unpermitted ADU or an unfinished basement can be hard for a financed buyer to close on. With no lender involved, the condition of the house is between you and us.

faqs.q: What county is Eagle Mountain in?
faqs.a: Utah County. Property taxes and recording go through the county offices in Provo.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Eagle Mountain?
faqs.a: November 30. Delinquent parcels are charged starting December 1.

faqs.q: Which school district will Eagle Mountain be in after 2027?
faqs.a: The Lake Mountain School District, which replaces Alpine School District on July 1, 2027 and also covers Saratoga Springs, Cedar Fort and Fairfield.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Eagle Mountain basement apartment short term?
faqs.a: No, not as an ADU. ADU rentals must run at least 30 consecutive days, and other short-term rentals owe a 1% transient room tax.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Utah County?
faqs.a: The standard fee is $40 per document, with $2 for each additional description over ten.
